transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
South African jurist Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize today for what the Norwegian
Committee said was her lifelong effort to promote international law.
NPR's Kate Bartlett reports, "Pillay started her career fighting apartheid and more recently
led a panel that found Israel committed genocide in Gaza."
Last year's Nobel Peace Prize winner, Maria Corina Machado, famously gave her prize to
President Trump, who has often said he deserved to win it.
On being informed she had won, this year's winner, Navi Pillay, joked she could follow
suit.
If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump.
Pillay's award comes amid a diplomatic low point between the U.S. and South Africa, which
has taken Israel to the International Court of Justice over genocide allegations.
President Cyril Ramaphosa has congratulated Pillay.
The 85-year-old is the fifth South African to win the Peace Prize, Kate Bartlett, NPR
News, Johannesburg.
The National Hurricane Center says Hurricane Isaias is a powerful Category 3 storm.
Its top sustained winds are now at 120 miles per hour.
The storm could hit the Gulf Coast of Alabama and the Florida Panhandle late tonight or
early tomorrow morning.
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis says his state is preparing.
Now we know that this is going to be a major event in one way or another.
There's going to be major impacts throughout the Florida Panhandle.
Everyone has understood that and everyone's really been working together to make sure that
we are ready to go.
Hurricane Isaias is more than 140 miles south of the Florida Panhandle.
Forecasters warned the storm could drop 4 to 8 inches of rain after it makes landfall.
Some areas could get a foot.
A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent shot an immigrant in New York City late
yesterday.
A young boy was in the man's car at the time.
Police say the wounded man is conscious and was treated at a nearby hospital.
Steve Kastenbaum reports from New York this triggered protests and calls for ICE to leave
the city.
Police pushed back protesters as they surrounded a law enforcement vehicle trying to leave
upper Manhattan where the shooting took place.
Its window had been shattered.
In a written statement, Mayor Zara Mamdani called the shooting "an unconscionable and
incredibly serious situation" and he demanded that the president end all ICE enforcement
actions in New York.
Governor Kathy Hochul said she expressed outrage in a call with President Trump.
The Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that ICE agents were attempting
to arrest a man from the Dominican Republic with a prior criminal conviction and several
arrests.
They didn't say why he was shot.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Kastenbaum in New York.
This is NPR.
And some federal fuel relief measures, rising gas prices, continue to put strain on drivers.
That's especially true for those who depend on diesel fuel.
From Mississippi Public Radio Elise Katrine Gregg reports.
At a gas station in Jackson, U.S. Senate candidate Scott Cologne called for a temporary suspension
of the federal gas tax and a permanent stopgap for diesel relief.
He was joined by Arthur Payton, who owns a family trucking company based in Jackson,
but they haul across the country.
Payton says the price spikes are costing drivers up to $700 more every week in gas expenses.
The diesel cost at the pump now is averaging $6.30.
That's about a $2.50 increase in just six-month period.
And it's hard to recover those additional expenses in a short period of time.
Payton says they've started doing their own maintenance work on trucks to cut costs.
For NPR News, I'm Elise Katrine Gregg in Jackson, Mississippi.
The NFL has joined New Jersey in asking the U.S. Supreme Court to let states regulate
sports betting.
The case stems from a dispute over prediction markets, such as Kelshi.
The Pro Football League argues this is gambling.
Kelshi argues these exchanges are financial swaps and only the federal government should
regulate them.
Officials in France say two stolen paintings by Renoir have been located.
They have been taken from a museum in southern France.
The mayor of the town says six people allegedly connected with the heist have been arrested.
The paintings were among the most valuable in the museum.
This is NPR.

topics.text: South African jurist Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize for promoting international law
Hurricane Isaias strengthens to Category 3, threatens Gulf Coast of Alabama and Florida Panhandle
ICE agent shoots immigrant in New York City; protests erupt, mayor demands ICE withdrawal
Rising diesel fuel prices strain truck drivers; average price now $6.30 per gallon
NFL joins New Jersey asking Supreme Court to let states regulate sports betting
Two stolen Renoir paintings located in southern France; six arrested in connection with heist
